target_customer: Employers, mostly large tech and corporate offices, that pay for workplace food, snacks and wellbeing services
problem: Office workers struggle to eat healthily at work, and employers lack a simple way to supply healthy food and wellness programs.
business_model: B2B recurring service contracts for pantry stocking, micro markets, catering and wellbeing classes

founders.name: Michael Heinrich
education: Stanford (Threshold Venture Fellow, OnTrack Innovation Scholar)
UC Berkeley (summa cum laude, Phi Beta Kappa)
founders.background_notes: Per his YC profile: technical product management and software engineering at SAP and Microsoft, then consulting or finance roles. Company site says his childhood time in his grandmother's garden in Germany inspired the company.

technical_complexity.rationale: The core is operations and supply chain; the AI and IoT claims on the YC page concern kiosks and analytics layered on a mostly logistics business.

defensibility.rationale: Recurring office contracts and kiosk placements create some stickiness, but sourcing food and snacks has low barriers and many local rivals.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent copied it in sources found. The company grew by acquiring others (Byte in 2020, LeanBox in 2021, Welnys in 2022) and was itself acquired by HUNGRY in 2025.

market_need_then: Employers at large tech companies offered free food as a perk; the founder cites his own difficulty eating healthily during long office hours and research linking healthy eating to engagement. No dated market sizing was found.

branding.name_origin: garten is the German word for garden; the founder's childhood time in his grandmother's garden in Germany is the stated inspiration (company site). The earlier name Oh My Green was chosen for the original healthy food business; no source gives its origin.
branding.domain_note: Now uses garten.co, not an exact .com

identity.logo: New logo introduced with the 2020 rebrand; details not examined
identity.visual_style: Nutrition and sustainability tier ranking on products

branding.brand_signature: Five tier nutrition and sustainability ranking of products

rebrands.why: To align with its nutrition heritage and its aim to be a wellbeing provider, not just food (trade press, 2020).

brand_strength.rationale: Named blue chip clients (Apple, Google, Stripe, Nike) and trade press coverage of acquisitions and the rebrand, but no evidence of consumer virality or a distinctive asset beyond the tier ranking.

pivots.from: Healthy snack and food delivery for offices (Oh My Green)
pivots.to: Broader workplace wellbeing including cafes, markets and classes (garten)
pivots.why: Company said the new name matched its wellbeing vision and nutrition heritage.

outcome_analysis: Oh My Green sold healthy office food to large corporate clients, raised a $20M seed in October 2018, rebranded to garten in 2020 and expanded by buying Byte, LeanBox and Welnys. With 201 people listed on YC it reached real scale, and HUNGRY acquired it in 2025, valued by Axios at $325M for the combined HUNGRY business. Price paid for garten and whether investors made money were not found.
notes: Competitor search found no sources dated near the 2016 batch, so the list is empty. The HUNGRY press release page returned 403; its date (2025-07-16) and the April 2025 report come from search results, so the exit date is given as year only. Axios Pro reports HUNGRY valued at $325M after the deal, not the price of garten. Total funding is inconsistent: CB Insights lists $27.62M over 6 rounds, Craft lists $20M. Only the $20M seed (October 2018, reported by TechCrunch) is recorded; the TechCrunch page was identified from search results and not opened. Acquisition by Byte Foods (2020) is from garten site links and trade press, not detailed here.
